claims.statement: The repository hosts the replacement marketplace at industria24.com.br, implemented with a strict-TypeScript Next.js 16 App Router application; public routes live at the root of src/app while route groups separate administrative, seller, affiliate, and partner areas, and reusable business logic/integrations live in src/lib.
The MCP server is an independently packaged Node service in mcp-server with its own build and start scripts; its standalone HTTP listener defaults to 0.0.0.0:3333 and serves the /mcp endpoint.
Contributors must consult the relevant installed Next.js documentation under node_modules/next/dist/docs before writing Next.js code because the repository's Next version has breaking changes.

The root package provides npm commands for development, production build/start, ESLint, and one-shot Vitest testing, and Vitest discovers Node-environment tests in src and scripts according to its configuration.

The root environment template requires public Supabase URL and anon-key configuration, keeps the service-role key out of client configuration, and the project ignores local environment files while retaining .env.example.
Data-backed routes without a configured .env.local deliberately use an explicit error state rather than a mock-data visual fallback.

The MCP service requires server-side Supabase URL and service-role credentials, uses an anon key for the buyer-authenticated checkout tool, defaults writes to disabled, and accepts module-level write enablement plus an optional allowed-origin list.
MCP partners use i24_ bearer tokens rather than database credentials; the service validates and scopes those tokens, limits writes to the token's store and enabled modules, and audits writes.
CI runs Gitleaks, root dependency installation followed by lint/build and high-or-higher npm audit, Vitest, and a check that migration files do not share a four-digit numeric prefix.

The marketplace Next configuration applies site-wide security headers, rewrites the Uber Direct webhook compatibility URL to its /api route, and configures Sentry source-map upload settings for builds without requiring them for the build to proceed.
The root layout installs global cart and affiliate-selection providers and a chat widget, making those cross-cutting UI features available around routed page content.
Database schema evolution is migration-led in supabase/migrations, and the repository contains SQL E2E and RLS regression tests under supabase/tests.

The operations dashboard is a separately packaged Next.js application in dashboard-ops with independent development, lint, build, and start commands; its configuration fixes Next output tracing to that directory.
The operations dashboard polls its GitHub, Vercel, Sentry, and cron API routes every 30 seconds to display operational data.

The MCP HTTP application handles each POST to /mcp statelessly, authenticates its Bearer token before building a per-request server, returns a 401 JSON-RPC error when authentication fails, and rejects GET and DELETE session requests with 405.
The MCP checkout client uses the Supabase anon key and the buyer's supplied access token so that checkout runs under that buyer's RLS identity rather than the service role.
